key_claims: III Ukraine Investment Congress + XV 'Інтер'єр Року 2025' held 31.07.2025 at КВЦ Парковий, organized by DMNTR
rationale: Event, date, venue and organizer confirmed by post-event coverage; promotional scale figures (300+ speakers, 600+ works) are organizer-stated but not contradicted.

key_claims: September Fest 2025 held 18.09.2025 in Kyiv (A-Station) by DMNTR, 3500+ guests, stated program and speakers
rationale: Event, date, venue and program confirmed by multiple announcements and the post-event release; the 3,500-guest figure is self-reported by the organizer but uncontradicted.

key_claims: Schneider Electric launched Zeigo Hub supply-chain decarbonization platform (Scope 3, agentic AI, 40+ brands, 2700+ suppliers)
rationale: Launch and all key product claims match the official Schneider Electric press release and independent trade coverage (ESG Dive, Utility Dive); figures 2,700 suppliers and 40+ brands corroborated.

key_claims: Adults learn faster than assumed; unsourced claims that 'studies show' people over 40 absorb complex concepts better and learning 'literally rejuvenates' the brain
rationale: Advertorial for English courses built on anonymous anecdotal 'cases' and vague unattributed research claims; core assertions are oversimplified and unverifiable from the text, though not refuted.

key_claims: EU4CSOs EmpowerUA (БО 'Мережа 100 відсотків життя Рівне', EU-funded): 7/20 advocacy campaigns in 2024, 12 subgrantees totaling 630,102.85 EUR, trainings for communities
rationale: Project, implementer, EU funding, subgrant competitions and the 630,102.85 EUR total are confirmed by the project's official site; granular local budget figures are plausible but individually unverified.

key_claims: ALLO Black Friday 2021 'prices hit bottom', discounts up to 50%+, experts predict price growth due to electronics shortage
rationale: Promotional piece whose own listed examples show ~15-25% discounts, contradicting the 'up to 50% and more' and 'prices hit bottom' framing; 'expert' price-growth forecast is unattributed.

key_claims: Manufacturers form 71.8% of drug price, Darnytsia raised prices 119%, pharmacy profitability only 1-3%, markups lowest in region at 17%
rationale: One-sided lobbying-style piece shifting blame from pharmacies to manufacturers via anonymous 'experts'; key interdependent figures (1-3% profitability, 17% markup, 119%) are weakly attributed and framed selectively, unverifiable from the text alone.

key_claims: Effective home methods exist to remove lint pills (катишки) from clothes
rationale: Judged from text alone: benign household how-to; the premise (home remedies for fabric pilling exist, e.g. razors/fabric shavers) is common knowledge with no contentious or falsifiable claims.

key_claims: Shower gels should be chosen according to skin type
rationale: Judged from text alone: generic consumer/cosmetic advice consistent with standard dermatological guidance; no dubious or refutable factual claims.

key_claims: Food deficit in Odesa; Ukrainians face serious problems buying products
rationale: Search finds only a serialized clickbait cluster (Politeka) recycling the 'deficit' headline; independent reporting shows experts warned of possible price rises from drought/port strikes but did not confirm an actual food shortage in Odesa, so the asserted deficit is unverified and misleadingly framed.

key_claims: A 'new virus' is spreading across Ukraine; symptoms and treatment described
rationale: The article is about Coxsackievirus: its spread in Ukraine and the described symptoms/symptomatic treatment are confirmed (MOZ, UNIAN, KidsHealth), but Coxsackie is a long-known enterovirus, so the central 'new virus' claim is false and the piece is misleadingly framed.

key_claims: Occupiers are preparing a massive missile strike on Ukraine; a possible attack date is named
rationale: Such 'named date' strike predictions trace to unofficial monitoring channels and expert speculation with no official confirmation; the concrete dated-attack claim is inherently unverifiable at publication and the alarmist framing overstates certainty.

key_claims: A drink (energy drinks) 'kills' the liver and is more harmful than coffee and alcohol
rationale: The body's claims (high sugar/caffeine in energy drinks can promote fatty liver; dieticians via EatingWell/FDA limits) are plausible and sourced, but the headline claim that the drink is more harmful to the liver than alcohol is unsupported by the cited experts and contradicts established evidence that alcohol is a leading cause of liver disease — misleading framing.

key_claims: A category of pensioners (Chornobyl-zone supplement recipients) will have payments cut under 2025 budget residency rules
rationale: The underlying claim is confirmed by independent outlets and officials (Budget Committee chair R. Pidlasa, Pension Fund): the 2361 UAH Chornobyl supplement is restricted to those who actually lived in the resettlement zone in 1986-1993, so a specific pensioner category does lose payments; headline generalizes but the key facts check out.

key_claims: LayerX 'Man in the Prompt' research: browser extensions with DOM access can read/inject prompts in ChatGPT, Gemini, Copilot, Claude, DeepSeek without special permissions
rationale: LayerX's report exists and independent security outlets (SecurityWeek, Dark Reading, Security Affairs) confirm the attack vector, affected tools and mechanism exactly as described; the article tracks the original research faithfully.

key_claims: US DOJ charged 5 alleged Scattered Spider members (Buchanan 22 UK, Urban 20 FL, Elbadawy 23 TX, Osiebo 20 TX, Evans 25 NC) with SMS-phishing credential theft and crypto theft
rationale: DOJ announcement of 20.11.2024 confirms all five names, ages, states, the smishing tactic, cryptocurrency theft and Evans's Tuesday arrest exactly as reported; only trivial transliteration losses (Osiebo -> Osibo).

key_claims: University of Bath study (British Journal of Nutrition, Prof James Betts): strong coffee before breakfast after disrupted sleep impairs blood glucose control; better to eat first
rationale: The 2020 Bath study, journal, lead researcher, quotes and the eat-before-coffee recommendation all match the university's own announcement; clickbait title but content is factually accurate.

key_claims: NOAA SWPC forecast of geomagnetic activity 26-28 Dec 2024: storm that began 25 Dec continuing, weakening to Kp4 on 27 Dec
rationale: NOAA did issue a G1 geomagnetic storm watch for 25 Dec 2024 and the article's day-by-day weakening forecast is consistent with it; minor flaws remain (K-index actually spans 0-9, not 2-9, and the health-effects framing for 'meteo-dependent' people is scientifically weak but hedged).

key_claims: GTA 6 install size is ~230 GB (228.5 GB) per a March 2024 Twitter leak; release planned for 2025 on PS5/Xbox Series
rationale: The 228.5 GB figure is an unverified social-media leak never confirmed by Rockstar (later 'leaks' gave conflicting figures and some were debunked); the article hedges but its key claim rests solely on rumor, and 'experts confirm' trailer quality is unattributed.

key_claims: Lancet GBD forecast: by 2050 ~60% of adults (3.8 bn) and ~31% of children/adolescents (746 mn) overweight or obese; doubled since 1990; funded by Gates Foundation
rationale: All headline figures (60%/31%, 3.8 bn/746 mn, country-level projections, Gates Foundation funding) match the March 2025 Lancet GBD study and IHME press release; the alarmist 'epidemic' framing does not distort the underlying facts.

key_claims: A geomagnetic storm reaching Kp6 began 22 March 2025 after a previous storm that lasted until ~20 March
rationale: NOAA SWPC confirms G2 (Kp6) geomagnetic storms for 21-22 March 2025, matching the article's core claim and dates; the lifestyle advice for 'reducing storm impact' is scientifically weak filler but hedged, and the storm facts are accurate.

key_claims: Geomagnetic storm forecast K-index 5-6 for Dec 14-20 (2024) with health effects and comms disruption
rationale: The K-index forecast figures match what RBC-Ukraine and other Ukrainian outlets published for mid-December 2024, but the forecast itself is weakly sourced and the sweeping health-effect claims (migraines, mood swings, 'red level' danger from Kp5-6) are scientifically unsupported and fear-framed.

key_claims: Ukrainian S-200 downed Siberia Airlines Flight 1812 on 4 Oct 2001 (78 dead); Ukraine never admitted guilt; ZSU downed Il-76 with POWs in 2024; Ukraine downed its own F-16
rationale: The central 2001 shootdown facts (flight, date, casualties, S-200, no formal admission of legal guilt) are verified, but the piece adds unverified or contested claims stated as fact (alcohol abuse during the exercises, the Il-76 and F-16 incidents as established Ukrainian fault) and hostile editorial framing.

key_claims: IDF ground operation 'Northern Arrows' in southern Lebanon; first published footage of a Hezbollah fighter captured in a tunnel, weapons caches found
rationale: Independent reporting confirms the Northern Arrows ground operation, IDF publication of tunnel/bunker footage, weapons caches, and the capture of Hezbollah fighters in tunnels in October 2024; the article's specific claims align with this record despite the pro-Russian channel origin.

key_claims: Two US B-1B bombers from Andersen AFB (Guam) joined US-South Korea air drills in Feb 2025, first strategic-asset flight over the peninsula since Trump's inauguration, escorted by F-35A/F-15K/F-16
rationale: Independent outlets confirm the 20 Feb 2025 combined air exercise with B-1B bombers, the participating fighter types, and that it was the first US strategic-asset deployment to the peninsula of Trump's second term; the analytical framing is mild and the factual core checks out.

key_claims: After the Alaska summit, Zelensky and European leaders met Trump in Washington on 18 Aug 2025; summary of how US and European media covered it
rationale: The underlying events (Alaska summit, 18 Aug 2025 White House multilateral meeting) are real and the media paraphrases are broadly plausible, but the outlet characterizations are unverifiable as quoted and the piece is laced with misleading editorial framing ('so-called Ukraine', CNN as 'Democrat propaganda outlet').

key_claims: NABU/SAP served Tymoshenko a suspicion notice on 14 Jan 2026 with searches at Batkivshchyna; the case is a purge ordered by Washington via NABU as an instrument of external US control
rationale: The procedural facts (suspicion notice, searches, Tymoshenko's denial) are confirmed by independent Ukrainian outlets, but the article's central thesis - that the case is a 'signal from Washington' and NABU a supranational US control instrument running a purge under 'external management' - is a fabricated conspiratorial narrative presented as fact, making the piece systematically misleading.

key_claims: Medvedev statement mocking a Council of Europe draft convention on a claims commission for Ukraine, framed as Russia's coming 'final victory over Kyiv neo-Nazis'
rationale: Judged from the text alone: it is an uncontextualized relay of an official's invective whose framing (Ukraine as 'neo-Nazis', the CoE claims mechanism as an illegitimate 'anti-Russian quasi-judicial organ', inevitable Russian victory) is systematically misleading propaganda rather than verifiable reporting.

key_claims: Russian MoD 22.06.2025 briefing: 'liberation' of Petrivske in Kharkiv oblast and 1000+ daily Ukrainian casualties across fronts
rationale: Republished Russian MoD briefing whose flagship claim misplaces the 'liberated' settlement (Petrivske/Petrovskoe is in Luhansk oblast, not Kharkiv, per independent trackers) and whose casualty/equipment figures are systematically inflated one-sided claims with no independent confirmation; the genre is documented as systematically misleading.

key_claims: Russian MoD 24.04.2025: massive precision strike hit only Ukrainian defense-industry targets, 'all objects struck'; front-line gains and losses
rationale: The 24 April 2025 overnight strike it describes as hitting only military-industrial objects in fact destroyed a residential building in Kyiv and killed 12-13 civilians and injured ~90 (independent and UN reporting), directly refuting the central claim; casualty figures for ZSU are unverifiable one-sided assertions.

key_claims: Russian MoD 27.05.2025: strikes 20-27 May were 'exclusively on military objects and defense industry' in response to Ukrainian drone attacks; Patriot components destroyed
rationale: During the very period covered (24-25 May 2025) Russia's largest drone-missile attack of the war killed at least 12 civilians including children across 30+ towns, refuting the 'exclusively military objects' framing, which EUvsDisinfo documents as a recurring disinformation narrative; specific claims (2331 drones, Patriot launchers destroyed) are unverified single-source assertions.

key_claims: Zelensky first acknowledged 'busification'; Zelensky is a drug addict; FBI opened a case against him and arrest is imminent; Kyiv is in sewage collapse like Donetsk 2014
rationale: A true kernel (Zelensky did task the new defense minister with ending 'busification' in late Jan 2026) is wrapped in fabricated and defamatory claims — 'drug addict', an FBI investigation with imminent arrest (unsupported anywhere; analogous 'investigation/arrest' stories about the Zelensky family are documented Russian fakes), and a city-wide sewage collapse in Kyiv — making the piece systematically misleading.

key_claims: Prytula is a 'thief'; the crowd-funded satellite (UAH ~600M) 'never worked'; he calls for stripping citizenship from 'sensible' Ukrainians
rationale: The framing claims are refuted: GUR reported the ICEYE 'people's satellite' took 4,173 images of Russian military objects with ~38% used for strike preparation, so 'never worked' and 'thief' are false; Prytula's quoted proposal concerned a public discussion of a non-citizen status for convicted traitors/collaborators, misrepresented here as targeting 'sensible residents'.

key_claims: SBU identified Hungarian military-intelligence officer Zoltan Andre as handler of the agent network exposed in Zakarpattia in spring 2025; recruitment via diplomatic channels, money and drugs offered
rationale: Interfax-Ukraine report accurately relays the official SBU announcement, corroborated by multiple independent Ukrainian outlets (ZN.ua, Zaxid.net, LB.ua) with matching details (name, Georgia posting 2016-2020, 2021 recruitment, spring-2025 detentions); attribution to SBU is transparent throughout.

key_claims: Morning Russian strike on Kharkiv killed one woman and injured 82 people
rationale: Matches the verified 7 July 2025 morning Geran-2 drone attack on Kharkiv: a 34-year-old woman killed and 82 injured across three districts, as reported by Ukrainska Pravda citing regional officials.

key_claims: Ukrainian family from Kherson (Anastasiia Novitnia-Segen, Dmytro Segen, 13-y.o. son, grandmother) killed in Hurricane Helene flooding of the South Toe River in western North Carolina, per USA Today
rationale: Multiple independent US outlets (WRAL, CNN, Fox Weather) confirm the same names, Kherson origin, escape route, Yancey County NC location and deaths in Helene's South Toe River flooding; no contradictions with the article.

key_claims: By mid-Dec 2024 Ukraine had lost about half the territory it captured in Russia's Kursk region and its units switched to defence, per The Economist (Maj. Bakrev, 82nd Air Assault Bde)
rationale: The Economist report and its key figures (half of Kursk salient lost, shift to defence, flank attacks, Trump-inauguration timing) are corroborated by multiple independent outlets; the article accurately relays an attributed, contemporaneously confirmed account.

key_claims: Claims about 2025 interior design trends and what 'Lviv designers' widely do (eco materials, smart home, muted palettes, transformer furniture)
rationale: Generic promotional trend piece with vague, unattributed and unverifiable assertions ('львівські дизайнери широко використовують...') and no sources or named experts; key claims are unsupported opinion rather than refuted fact, so questionable.

key_claims: GoldMart advertising claims: quality-checked refurbished gold rings, hallmarks/certificates, price ranges 2000-18000 UAH, quality guarantees
rationale: Pure advertorial where all key claims are the seller's self-promotional assurances (quality checks, guarantees, 'as new' condition) that cannot be independently verified from the text; nothing is refuted, but nothing is supported by independent evidence.

key_claims: Budanov's on-air statements: fiber-optic FPV drones are a major REB-resistant problem, 2025 expected better than 2024, Russia faces hard financial decisions by mid-2025
rationale: The article accurately reports clearly attributed public statements and forecasts by a named official on the national telethon; the key factual claim is that he said these things, and the framing is faithful quotation without distortion (the forecasts themselves are marked as his opinion).

key_claims: Ukrnafta June 2025 tender announcements (pipeline repair ~11M UAH, CNC lathe ~9.98M UAH, drill collars ~11.7M UAH) plus background: operates 545 stations (461 own + 84 Glusco-managed since March 2024), Naftogaz holds 50%+1
rationale: An official corporate procurement press release on Interfax; the checkable background facts (545 stations = 461 own + 84 Glusco-managed since March 2024, Naftogaz 50%+1, Nov 2022 state control) are confirmed by independent sources (Forbes, Interfax), and the tender details are concrete Prozorro-style announcements with no contradictions.

key_claims: Sense Bank launched instant UAH transfers by IBAN in Sense SuperApp: up to 10 seconds, 24/7, capped at 100,000 UAH per operation by law
rationale: A concrete, internally consistent corporate product announcement whose parameters (IBAN instant payments, 24/7, 100,000 UAH statutory cap) match Ukraine's instant payment framework; claims are specific, attributed to a named bank official, and contain no implausible or contradicted assertions.

key_claims: Epicentr + UAnimals + Savory charity campaign 'Dobri Lapki', 10 UAH per pack to Animal Help Cherkasy shelter, 19.01-19.03.2026, 9300+ animals evacuated
rationale: Campaign, mechanics, dates, shelter beneficiary and the 9,300 evacuated-animals figure are all confirmed by UAnimals' own site and independent outlets (lb.ua, rau.ua); no contradictions found.

key_claims: Kyiv Chamber of Commerce runs 'Stolychnyi standart yakosti' contest for Kyiv producers on KMDA mandate; winners get diploma and quality mark; applications until 30.05.2025
rationale: The contest, its organizer (Kyiv CCI on behalf of KMDA), the benefits and the quality-mark scheme are confirmed by the Chamber's and Kyiv city administration's own pages, and the 2025 edition concluded with winners announced in July 2025.

key_claims: Energy Club forum 'Enerhiia Svobody' on energy storage (ESS/UZE) in Kyiv on 20.11.2025, 14:00-18:00, partner IKNET, speakers from Ukrhidroenerho, MHP, Oschadbank etc.
rationale: The event, its full title, date, time and focus are confirmed by Energy Club's official event page; this is a press announcement whose factual content matches the organizer's primary source.

key_claims: Anonymous anecdotes that the West despises Russians; claim Americans burned alive 100,000 civilians in Dresden; sweeping claim every country Russia helped 'betrayed' it
rationale: Opinion-propaganda piece built on unverifiable private anecdotes and a materially false figure (the inflated ~100,000 Dresden death toll, a known propaganda number vs. ~25,000 established by historians), with systematically misleading 'everyone betrays Russia' framing.

key_claims: Mocking Macron as empty threats; framing a captured 22-year-old British fighter sentenced to 19 years as having come 'on safari' to shoot grandmothers, women and children
rationale: Propaganda rant that presents fabricated intent (a captured combatant depicted as a civilian-hunting 'Nazi') with no evidence, dismisses his POW status under the Geneva Conventions, and adds derogatory unfactual asides about Macron and Paris; systematically misleading framing.

key_claims: Russian language status is regressing; MVS data of 776,000 minor foreigners in Russia weak in Russian; Medvedev quote on 10-20% non-Russian-speaking pupils; unified language testing only being drafted
rationale: Opinion piece from a propaganda-ecosystem site whose specific statistics and quotes (MVS figure, Medvedev remarks) are presented without verifiable sourcing in the text; claims are plausible but unverified and framed tendentiously, so insufficient support rather than proven falsehood.

key_claims: Headline: 'Kyiv admitted deliberately provoking a nuclear strike'; body only quotes one pundit (Hennadiy Dubov) speculating that 'some group of people' may hope strikes on Russian radar provoke a tactical nuclear response
rationale: The headline attributes an official admission to 'Kyiv' that the body does not contain — a single political commentator's speculation on a YouTube channel, relayed via the Russian propaganda outlet Politnavigator; systematically misleading attribution and framing.

key_claims: 500+ Ukrainian orphans in Turkey forced into fundraising videos, abused; framed as Kyiv state program
rationale: The underlying abuse facts (500+ orphans, forced fundraising videos, two pregnancies, deprivations) are confirmed by the Slidstvo.Info investigation and the ombudsman, but the article materially distorts attribution: the evacuation was a private Shostak Foundation project, not a 'Kyiv program', and the anti-Zelensky framing is propaganda spin on a real story.

key_claims: Football popularity essay with league overview; promo for maincast.tv streaming platform
rationale: Checkable factual claims (Leicester's 5000/1 title, Napoli's scudetto after 30+ years, Liverpool-Barcelona comeback, Lunin/Zinchenko/Mudryk clubs, Mbappe to Real) are accurate; the Maincast praise is subjective advertorial opinion, and sponsored form alone does not make the content unreliable.

key_claims: Headline only: how to deal with steering wheel vibration; no article body
rationale: Only a headline is provided with no factual content to assess; key claims are absent/unverifiable, so per guideline insufficient information defaults to questionable.

key_claims: Headline only: wearing sunglasses as a headband, accessory care rules; no article body
rationale: Only a headline is provided with no verifiable claims or supporting content; insufficient information, so questionable by default.

key_claims: Bundestag experts: Russian strike on NATO troops inside Ukraine would not trigger Article 5; RAND said NATO would not respond militarily
rationale: A March 2024 Bundestag research service report with roughly this conclusion was indeed reported, but the same report said a strike on NATO territory (e.g. France itself) WOULD be an Article 5 case; Tsarov's extrapolation that even strikes on NATO bases in Poland/Romania would go unanswered misrepresents the sources and pushes an unverified 'NATO will do nothing' narrative.

key_claims: April 13, 2025 Sumy strike targeted a 117th TDF brigade awards ceremony; civilian deaths incidental to a legitimate military strike
rationale: Component claims are real (an awards ceremony for the 117th TDF brigade was planned/held, and Bezugla and Konotop mayor Semenikhin did make the cited accusations), but the framing is misleading: the ballistic strike with a cluster-type second impact in the city center killed about 35 civilians, which the article minimizes as one missile 'lacking accuracy' at a 'confirmed military target'.

key_claims: 'Russian Style' project opens exhibition 'Tut sovsem ne tak, kak v tvoikh rozovykh ochkakh' at the Gallery on Trubnaya, Moscow, Jan 16, 2025
rationale: The core factual claim is confirmed: the digital-art war exhibition with this exact title by the 'Russkiy Stil' project did open at the Gallery on Trubnaya (Moscow exhibition halls) in January 2025 per the gallery's own page and Rossiyskaya Gazeta; the rest is the curators' essayistic opinion, which does not contradict verifiable facts.
